name: Collect and validate smart meter data
summary: Every day the utility's smart meter network collects hourly reads from about 352,000 meters and sends them to the province's Meter Data Management/Repository (MDM/R), run by the IESO as Smart Metering Entity, which validates and estimates the data and later returns billing quantities. A team of meter data analysts works the exceptions the next working day: meters that stopped communicating, reads that failed validation, mismatches between the billing system and the repository, meter exchanges and failed billing quantity requests. Work is slow because each exception needs a look at interval history, outage records and account changes, weekend cycles wait for Monday, and every unresolved meter risks an estimated bill, which the OEB limits to two a year per customer.

baseline.org_archetype: A municipally owned Ontario distributor of about 350,000 customers with a mesh AMI network, a local meter data tool, a CIS, and the provincial MDM/R.
baseline.notes: One case is one daily read cycle: all meters' reads for one calendar day, from collection to release of billing quantities and hand-off of unresolved exceptions.

trigger: Midnight: the AMI head-end starts collecting the previous day's interval reads.
end_state: The day's billing quantities are released to billing, and every exception is either fixed, sent to the field or handed to billing exceptions.

volume.seasonality: One cycle every day of the year. Exception counts rise after storms and long outages (meters lose communication), on daylight-saving changes and after mass meter exchange campaigns.

evidence.note: One cycle per calendar day.
Org file has 8 meter data analysts; about 5 to 6 FTE on daily read exceptions, the rest on billing exceptions, sampling data and reporting. Loaded cost from the organisation file (wage x 1.40).
Weekly backlog review and escalations. Loaded cost from the organisation file (wage x 1.40).

systems.name: Provincial Meter Data Management/Repository (IESO Smart Metering Entity) portal
Local meter data management and validation tool
Mobile workforce management and field tablets

steps.name: Collect overnight interval reads
steps.description: The AMI head-end polls about 352,000 smart meters through the mesh network and collectors after midnight and stores the 24 hourly register and interval reads for the previous day. Meters that do not answer are marked missing for the retry pass.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from how Ontario distributors ran the AMI head-end, the provincial MDM/R and a local exception tool in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Re-poll missing meters
steps.description: The head-end runs its scheduled retry passes on meters and collectors that did not report, and fills gaps from meter memory where the meter answers late. Reads still missing after the last pass stay as gaps for the provincial repository to estimate.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from how Ontario distributors ran the AMI head-end, the provincial MDM/R and a local exception tool in 2019-2022. Collection and retry windows of four to seven hours.

steps.name: Transmit reads to the provincial repository
steps.description: The head-end formats the day's reads into the repository's interface file and transmits it to the IESO Smart Metering Entity's Meter Data Management/Repository (MDM/R). Transmission failures raise an alert to the OT on-call specialist.

error.defect_description: File rejected or late, so the day loads with missing intervals.

evidence.note: The MDM/R processes reads from over 5.1 million smart meters for all Ontario distributors daily (sme).

steps.name: Repository validates, estimates and edits reads
steps.description: The MDM/R runs validation, estimation and editing (VEE) on each meter's day: sum checks between interval and register reads, gap and spike checks, and estimation of missing intervals. It returns read status and a list of failed and estimated meters to the distributor.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 393/07: the Smart Metering Entity specifies and performs VEE to produce billing quantity data

evidence.note: The SME reports meter-read and billing-quantity service levels and adjusts VEE thresholds (for example the 2021 Small General Service sum-check threshold change) (sme). Processing time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Load results and build exception worklists
steps.description: The local meter data tool imports the repository's VEE results, the head-end's communication status and the CIS account list, and builds worklists: non-communicating meters, failed validations, synchronization mismatches and meters estimated several days running.

next.condition: read day falls on Saturday or Sunday

evidence.note: Author's estimate from how Ontario distributors ran the AMI head-end, the provincial MDM/R and a local exception tool in 2019-2022. Two of seven read days fall on a weekend.

steps.name: Hold weekend cycle until Monday
steps.description: Analysts work office hours, so exception worklists built on Saturday and Sunday wait for Monday. The OT on-call specialist reacts only to head-end or transmission alarms; ordinary meter exceptions are left in the queue.

evidence.note: Office-hours analysts; weekend worklists wait one to two days.

steps.name: Review daily read performance
steps.description: A meter data analyst opens the daily dashboard in the local tool and the MDM/R portal, checks the read success rate, the count of 'No Data' and estimated meters, any collector outages and the age of open exceptions, and splits the day's worklists among the team.

error.defect_description: A collector outage is missed and its meters stay estimated another day.

evidence.note: The SME gives each distributor monthly performance reports and daily operational data and tracks 'No Data' responses that impede billing (sme).

steps.name: Work failed validations
steps.description: Two analysts go through meters that failed VEE: sum-check failures between interval and register reads, zero consumption on an active account, consumption on a vacant premise and reverse flow on a meter without generation. They compare the interval profile with history and the CIS account, edit or accept the estimate, or mark the meter for a field check.

error.defect_description: An edit or accepted estimate is wrong and flows to the bill.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from how Ontario distributors ran the AMI head-end, the provincial MDM/R and a local exception tool in 2019-2022. Two analysts for most of the day.

steps.name: Work non-communicating meters
steps.description: Two other analysts work meters with no reads for one or more days. They ping each meter from the head-end, check the outage management system for an outage or disconnection, look for a pattern by collector or street, and decide whether the cause is the network, the meter or the premise.

error.defect_description: A failed meter is diagnosed as a network problem and stays estimated.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from how Ontario distributors ran the AMI head-end, the provincial MDM/R and a local exception tool in 2019-2022. Runs alongside the validation work.

steps.name: Raise OT ticket for network fault
steps.description: When a cluster of meters behind one collector or relay stops reporting, the analyst opens a ticket for the OT specialists with the collector id, the affected meter count and the first missing hour, and follows up on the ticket the next day.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from how Ontario distributors ran the AMI head-end, the provincial MDM/R and a local exception tool in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Fix synchronization mismatches
steps.description: One analyst resolves records where the CIS and the MDM/R disagree: meter number, multiplier, rate class, or account status after a move-in, move-out or retailer switch. The analyst corrects the CIS or resubmits the master data so the repository can return billing quantities.

error.defect_description: A keyed multiplier or meter number is wrong.

evidence.note: The SME works with distributors on synchronization and data-submission quality, and fewer synchronization exceptions improve billing success (sme). Time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Process meter change records
steps.description: The same analyst checks the meter exchanges completed by technicians the day before: old meter final read, new meter initial read, dates and seal information. Clean records are sent to the MDM/R so the new meter's reads are accepted; incomplete ones go back to the metering supervisor.
outputs: meter change records sent to the MDM/R

error.defect_description: An exchange is synchronized with a wrong read, giving a spike on the next bill.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from how Ontario distributors ran the AMI head-end, the provincial MDM/R and a local exception tool in 2019-2022. About 100 exchanges a working day.

steps.name: Close exceptions from field results
steps.description: An analyst reads the results of completed field orders (meter replaced, premise vacant, tampering found, meter base repaired) and closes or updates the matching exceptions in the local tool and the CIS.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from how Ontario distributors ran the AMI head-end, the provincial MDM/R and a local exception tool in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Create field and meter orders
steps.description: For meters that need a visit the analyst creates the order in the CIS: a meter exchange for a failed or non-communicating meter, or a field investigation for suspected tampering, vacant premises or access problems, with the evidence attached.

error.defect_description: Order created with the wrong premise or reason.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from how Ontario distributors ran the AMI head-end, the provincial MDM/R and a local exception tool in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Review aged exceptions and backlog
steps.description: The metering supervisor reviews exceptions open more than five days, meters estimated close to the two-estimates-a-year limit and the field order backlog, and reassigns or escalates them with field services and IT.

control.basis: Distribution System Code estimated-billing limit: no more than two estimated bills to a customer in 12 months

evidence.note: Limit of two estimated bills in 12 months (bg2015); weekly review frequency is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Request billing quantities for the day's cycle
steps.description: In the evening batch the CIS sends billing quantity requests to the MDM/R for every account whose bill period ended, with the meter, period and rate structure.

evidence.note: Billing quantity requests and responses are a critical MDM/R service level (sme); batch timing is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Repository returns billing quantities
steps.description: The MDM/R aggregates each account's validated intervals into time-of-use or tiered billing quantities and returns them, or returns 'No Data' when the period is not billable yet.

evidence.note: 100% of billing quantity requests fulfilled on time in Q2 2021 (sme).

steps.name: Load responses and flag failures
steps.description: The CIS loads the responses and puts accounts with 'No Data', partial periods or failed sum checks on the billing quantity failure list for the analysts.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from how Ontario distributors ran the AMI head-end, the provincial MDM/R and a local exception tool in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Work billing quantity failures
steps.description: Next morning two analysts go through the failure list: they fix the master data, trigger a re-request after an edit, or decide that the period needs a manual estimate. Each account is checked against its estimate history so the customer does not receive a third estimated bill in a year.

error.defect_description: An account is re-requested without the underlying fix and fails again.

evidence.note: 'No Data' responses impede billing (sme); estimate limit (bg2015). Shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Edit or estimate reads in the repository
steps.description: For gaps the VEE could not fill, the analyst enters a manual estimate or edit in the MDM/R portal using the customer's own history or a like-day profile, records the reason code, and re-requests billing quantities.

error.defect_description: Manual estimate far from actual use, later corrected by a rebill.

control.basis: MDM/R VEE editing rules and Distribution System Code estimated-billing limits

evidence.note: Author's estimate from how Ontario distributors ran the AMI head-end, the provincial MDM/R and a local exception tool in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Refer unresolved accounts to billing
steps.description: The analyst lists accounts that metering cannot make billable today (meter needs a visit, long gap, disputed history) with the reason and expected fix date, and sends them to the billing exceptions queue so billing can hold or estimate the bill.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from how Ontario distributors ran the AMI head-end, the provincial MDM/R and a local exception tool in 2019-2022.

exceptions.name: Weekend read days
exceptions.description: Saturday and Sunday cycles are collected and validated automatically, but their exceptions wait for Monday, when analysts work three days of worklists.

exceptions.name: Collector or network outage
exceptions.description: A collector, relay or backhaul link fails and hundreds of meters stop reporting; the analyst raises an OT ticket and the meters are estimated until the network is repaired.

exceptions.name: Accounts not billable today
exceptions.description: Some accounts in the day's cycle cannot get billing quantities even after edits and are handed to billing exceptions to hold or estimate the bill.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from start of read collection to billing quantities released and exceptions dispositioned

evidence.note: Author's estimate: reads collected overnight, VEE by morning, exceptions worked the same working day, billing quantity failures the next morning; weekend cycles wait to Monday.

benchmarks.population: All Ontario distributors using the MDM/R

pain_points.description: 'No Data' billing quantity responses and synchronization mismatches between the CIS and the repository hold up bills until an analyst fixes master data and re-requests.

evidence.note: SME notes 'No Data' responses impede billing and that fewer synchronization exceptions improve billing success.

pain_points.description: Weekend exceptions wait until Monday, so a meter that fails on Friday night may be estimated for three days before anyone looks at it.

evidence.note: Office-hours staffing of the analyst team.

pain_points.description: Diagnosing a non-communicating meter needs the head-end, the outage system and the CIS open side by side; the knowledge of which collectors are flaky is held by a few experienced analysts.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from how Ontario distributors ran the AMI head-end, the provincial MDM/R and a local exception tool in 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: Customers near the two-estimates-a-year limit have to be tracked by hand across the metering and billing teams.

evidence.note: Limit introduced by the 2015 Distribution System Code amendments.

sources.title: Quarterly SME MDM/R Report, Issue 32.0 (2nd quarter 2021)
sources.publisher: IESO Smart Metering Entity (report to the Ontario Energy Board)
sources.supports: MDM/R scale (5,107,693 meters, all distributors, daily processing), billing quantity and meter read service levels, 'No Data' responses, synchronization exceptions, VEE threshold changes.

sources.title: Backgrounder: Monthly and Estimated Billing Changes to the Distribution System Code
sources.supports: Monthly billing from December 2016, bills based on actual reads, at most two estimated bills per customer in 12 months.

assumptions: The case is a daily cycle, so the simulation's touch time is the whole team's exception work for one day and the FTE check compares it with the analyst team.

The organisation file lists the IESO's 'validated_reads' as the trigger; in practice the cycle starts with the utility's own AMI head-end collection and the IESO repository returns validated data during the cycle. Meter change records, field results and account changes are standing inputs, not triggers, so they are listed under inputs.
Two analysts each work validation failures, non-communicating meters and billing quantity failures in parallel; these steps use people = 2 and concurrent_with so elapsed time is not added twice.
A storm surge is not modelled as extra cases because the number of daily cycles does not change; storms raise the exception count inside each cycle (for example after the May 2022 derecho).
The billing quantity request is placed in the evening batch and failures are worked the next morning, which puts about one working day between read collection and billable quantities.
Exception shares and step times are the author's estimates; no Ontario distributor publishes its daily exception counts.
